items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: (it was an Alvino Rey type band, you know)

ctx.x: Yeah. We would take a ship out into the River Humber, which was about three miles wide, and we’d take a bearing, and say that was true north, and in those days the compass was not magnetic, they worked with magnets, and adjust accordingly the magnets and what have you, to bring it truthfully into line, true north. I was doing that for about two years, and on one occasion I had to go and pick up some Admiralty Charts — not music charts — regular Admiralty Charts for the British Navy. They used to have corvettes…

adjuster’s apprentice I was earning 7 schillings and 6 pence a week, which in those days was like, oh maybe, it was like one dollar. Mr. Mendelsohn offered me 17 pounds a week. So guess what I did? It was rather a difficult decision because I was in love with a beautiful girl and it meant leaving her, and I thought oh, shall I do this? And then it occurred to me, I thought about it and I spoke to my parents of course, and they said, “Well you should try it and see how it works.” Those were the days when…
